response.why: batch: player A starts
2 Mountains + two haste creatures (Swiftspear turn 1 attacks immediately), Goblin Piker turn 2, and burn for reach. Textbook keep for mono-red aggro: solid mana, explosive early plays.
Always play your land first in main phase. I'll play a Mountain, then cast Monastery Swiftspear (haste) to attack immediately.
Cast Monastery Swiftspear (haste). It attacks immediately this turn. Early aggression is critical — save Lightning Bolt for face damage or creature removal later when it has more impact.

attack-all is vastly superior. Opponent has empty board—no crackback threat. The 1 damage from Swiftspear is real progress on our clock (5% of 20), and we tap out but so does the opponent. Aggro wins by racing damage; passing pressure on turn 1 when they're defenseless wastes tempo. Our tapped board doesn't matter—their board is also empty, and we have more creatures waiting.

Pass upkeep to reach my main phase. I need to play my second Mountain, cast Goblin Piker or my second Swiftspear, and continue applying pressure. Holding Lightning Bolt and Monstrous Rage for combat tricks and face burn is correct—casting them now in upkeep wastes their value and gives the opponent information. The opponent has a Forest but no visible threats yet; I should develop my board.
Pass to main phase. I just drew a card. Time to play my second land and cast Goblin Piker or my second Swiftspear to apply more pressure. Hold instants for later.

Play Mountain (land drop first). Then I'll have 2 untapped Mountains to cast creatures. I need to develop my board with Goblin Piker or my second Swiftspear to apply pressure while opponent is still empty.

Cast Monastery Swiftspear (R). It gets +1/+1 from prowess immediately, becoming 2/2 with haste. Cheaper than Goblin Piker, and I'll still have an untapped Mountain to follow up with Goblin Piker or hold priority. Building board while opponent has no creatures is the aggro plan.

Pass to reach combat. I have 1 Swiftspear ready to attack for 1 damage. I can't cast Goblin Piker (need 1R, only have 1 red mana available). After I attack and move to Postcombat Main, I'll have more options to evaluate further development or burn. Developing board pressure via attack is better than wasting Lightning Bolt on an empty board right now.

Pass to Combat. Excellent! I now have 2 Monastery Swiftspears (both untapped). With haste, they both attack this turn for 2 damage total. Opponent is still at 19 life with empty board—this is the time to apply maximum pressure. Accelerate the clock before they develop creatures.
Pass to Declare Attackers. I have 2 untapped Swiftspears ready to attack with haste. No reason to cast instants in Begin Combat when I can apply damage via attacking.

attack-all is vastly superior. Opponent has empty board (only Forest). We should maximize clock: 2 damage/turn wins in ~9 turns (19 life / 2 = 9.5) vs holding back at 1 damage/turn (~19 turns). Tapping both Swiftspears is safe since they have no crackback threat. Aggro wins by racing damage, not by playing defensively when ahead on board and the opponent is empty. Defend later if creatures show up.

Pass priority to Declare Blockers. I've already declared both Swiftspears as attackers. Opponent has no creatures to block with (only Forest). No need to pump or burn now—save Lightning Bolt for later removal or face damage. Let blocks resolve.

Pass to resolve combat. Opponent has no blockers (only Forest, no creatures). Both Swiftspears deal 1 damage each unblocked (2 total). Move to End Combat and Postcombat Main to evaluate further plays.

Pass to End Combat. Combat damage resolved—opponent at 17 life (took 2 from both Swiftspears). Move to Postcombat Main where I can play more creatures or evaluate further turns. We're ahead on tempo and the clock is ticking.
Pass to Postcombat Main. No instants needed in End Combat. I want to reach my main phase to play Goblin Piker or develop my board further before the opponent's turn.

Pass to End Step. I can't cast Goblin Piker (need 1R, only have 1R from untapped Mountain, but that pays for the R cost only—I need generic mana too). Lightning Bolt should be saved for removal or face damage. Monstrous Rage is a combat trick, best held until blockers are declared. Opponent is at 17 life. Let's see what they do on their turn.

Pass to end turn. I'll yield until my next turn to skip through the opponent's turn if they pass without developing (though likely they'll play creatures). Clock: 2 damage/turn from Swiftspears, opponent at 17 life = ~8 more turns to kill them.

Pass opponent's upkeep. It's their turn 4. I can cast instants if needed, but I should wait to see what they do first. If they play creatures, I can respond with removal or combat tricks. Holding Lightning Bolt and Monstrous Rage is better than casting them blind.

Pass. Opponent is in their Precombat Main on turn 4. They've cast Grizzly Bears (2/2, summoning sick). No immediate threat. I should hold my instants for when they matter—either for removal or combat tricks. Let their turn progress.
Pass opponent's Begin Combat. Their Grizzly Bears has summoning sickness and can't attack. They have no other creatures. They'll likely pass combat or declare no attackers. No instants needed here.
Pass. Opponent has only Grizzly Bears with summoning sickness—can't attack. They'll pass combat. I'll yield until my turn now.

Play Mountain (land drop first). Then I'll have 3 untapped Mountains in play + can tap 2 for Goblin Piker (1R = 2 mana). Opponent at 17 life with only summoning-sick Grizzly Bears. Time to build board pressure and close the game.

Cast Goblin Piker (1R = 2 mana, I have 3 untapped Mountains). Board is now: 2 Swiftspears + Goblin Piker = 5 power across 3 creatures. Next turn, I attack with 5 damage. Opponent at 17 life (3-4 more turns to kill with this clock). Building pressure while they develop.

Pass to Combat. I've developed my board with Swiftspears and Goblin Piker. Opponent at 17 life with only summoning-sick Grizzly Bears (can't block). Time to attack and apply damage. The clock is closing: with ~5 power attacking each turn, I can kill in ~3-4 turns.

Pass to Begin Combat. Board is now: 2 untapped Swiftspears + Goblin Piker (summoning sick, can't attack yet). Opponent's Grizzly Bears also summoning sick (can't attack). I'll attack with the 2 Swiftspears for 2 damage, bringing opponent to 15 life. Closing the race.
Pass to Declare Attackers. Ready to attack with both Swiftspears for 2 damage total. Opponent at 17 life, summoning-sick Grizzly Bears can't block or attack yet.

attack-all is the correct line despite blocked scenarios (leaves 1-2, score ~60). Unblocked (leaf 3, score 90) is phenomenal: 2 damage to opponent at 17 = 8.5-turn clock with both creatures tapped but opponent's Grizzly Bears still summoning sick, unable to punish us. Hold scenarios (68-75) are safer but less aggressive. Aggro must maximize pressure when opponent is tapped out.

Pass priority after declaring both Swiftspears as attackers. Move to Declare Blockers phase. Opponent's Grizzly Bears is summoning sick and can't attack, but can block. Ready to see if they block or let 2 damage through. Opponent at 17 life.
Pass priority during Declare Blockers. Opponent has Grizzly Bears summoning sick (can block but not attack). Opponent will decide whether to block my attacking Swiftspears. Proceed to combat damage.
Pass priority. Opponent is in their upkeep turn 6. Grizzly Bears no longer summoning sick (can now attack). Yield to my turn to continue applying pressure.

Leaf 0 (no block): I take 2 damage, opponent keeps Grizzly Bears = worst outcome. Leaf 1 (block Swiftspear): I lose 1/2 creature, opponent keeps 2/2 threat = medium; Grizzly Bears survives tapped but depletes my board. Leaf 2 (block Piker): I trade 2/1 for 2/2 Grizzly Bears, keep Swiftspear = good; removing threat is valuable. Leaf 3 (both block): I trade 1/2 Swiftspear but keep 2/1 Piker, kill 2/2 Grizzly Bears = best; Piker is a better attacker than Swiftspear and opponent loses key threat. Higher life-clock advantage with Piker untapped.

Cast Lightning Bolt for 3 damage (17→14). Opponent has no creatures and 3 Forests—no way to interact. Lightning Bolt is efficient mana usage (1R), deals unconditional damage, preserves Monstrous Rage for future combat tricks, and leaves mana open for next turn. Follow with Mountain and Piker attack for 5 total damage this turn.

Target player B (opponent at 17 life). Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage, bringing opponent to 14 life. Direct damage to the opponent progresses toward the win condition. Targeting own Piker or myself would be counterproductive.

Cast Monstrous Rage on Goblin Piker for 1R. Piker becomes 4/1 instead of 2/1, turning it into a 4-damage attacker. After playing Mountain from hand and attacking unblocked, Piker deals 4 damage to opponent (17→13, or 14→10 if Lightning Bolt hit). This maximizes damage output before passing to declare attackers.

Pass priority. Piker is already boosted to 4/1 via Monstrous Rage. I've cast my spells for the turn (Lightning Bolt + Monstrous Rage). Proceed to declare attackers and attack with Piker (4/1) for 4 damage. Land drop (Mountain in hand) can happen if needed during declare attackers or be saved for future turns.

Pass priority. Piker is now 5/2 with trample (from Monster aura enchantment). Move to declare attackers and attack for 5 unblocked damage, bringing opponent to 12 life. Opponent has no creatures and empty board, attack is undefendable.

Leaf 0 (attack-none): Passive play, no clock progress at 14 life. Bad strategy when opponent is injured. Leaf 1 (attack-all): Attack for 5 unblocked damage (Piker 5/2 with trample, opponent has no creatures). Brings opponent to 9 life, establishing 1.8-turn clock toward win condition. Aggro must maximize damage when opponent is defenseless. attack-all is overwhelming favorite.
Pass priority. Opponent's turn 8, upkeep phase. No actions needed. Opponent at 9 life is close to defeat. Yield to my turn for next attack phase.

Pass priority. Opponent's precombat main on turn 8. They've cast Rumbling Baloth (4/4, summoning sick). I cannot block it with tapped Piker. I cannot cast Bonebreaker Giant (needs 4R, only have 1R available). Hold remaining resources for my turn to continue applying clock pressure. Opponent at 9 life is close to defeat.
Pass priority. Begin Combat phase, opponent's turn 8. Rumbling Baloth has summoning sickness and cannot attack. Opponent will not attack this turn. Proceed through opponent's turn to my turn 9.
Pass priority. Opponent's Declare Attackers phase. Rumbling Baloth has summoning sickness and cannot attack. Opponent will not attack. Proceed to my turn 9 for lethal.

Play Mountain. Generates 4th land to unlock mana for Bonebreaker Giant (4R cost). Board becomes 4 untapped Mountains + Piker + Monster. After playing land, will tap Mountains and cast Bonebreaker Giant, then attack with Piker (3) + Giant (4) = 7 damage (9→2), guaranteeing lethal next turn. Opponent at 9 life is helpless with summoning-sick Rumbling Baloth.
Tap Mountain for red mana. Building toward 4R cost for Bonebreaker Giant. Have 4 Mountains available, tapping them sequentially to generate casting cost. First tap toward mana pool.
Tap second Mountain for red mana. Building toward 4R. Two mana accumulated, two more Mountains remaining untapped.
Tap third Mountain for red mana. Three mana accumulated, one Mountain remaining untapped. One more tap to reach 4R for Bonebreaker Giant.
Tap final Mountain for red mana. Reach 4R mana threshold for Bonebreaker Giant. All four Mountains now tapped, ready to cast.

Cast Dragon Fodder (1R). Creates two 1/1 Goblin tokens. Combined with Piker (3/2), attack for 5 damage (9→4 life), bringing opponent to 4. Opponent at 4 life with summoning-sick Rumbling Baloth still cannot interact. Lethal is guaranteed next turn. Note: Bonebreaker Giant (4R) should theoretically be castable with 4R available but is not shown in options; casting Dragon Fodder preserves mana flexibility.

Leaf 0 (no attack): Passive play, opponent stays at 9 life, summoning-sick Rumbling Baloth waits for turn 10. Bad tempo. Leaf 1 (Piker blocked): Lose Piker with no damage dealt, opponent stays at 9 life with intact Baloth. Worst-case scenario—trade creature for nothing. Leaf 2 (Piker unblocked): Deal 3 damage (9→6 life), maintain board tempo with Goblins and Bonebreaker Giant in hand. Piker taps but game state improves significantly. Goblins now free of summoning sickness next turn for multi-creature attack finish. Attack-all is clearly superior.

Evaluating from opponent's perspective (active blocker). Leaf 0 (no blocks): Best outcome for opponent—deals 4 damage (I'm at 16), keeps Rumbling Baloth alive at 4/4 to threaten future turns. Leaf 1 (Piker blocks): Loses Baloth entirely (1/4 health remains after 3 damage), I still cast Bonebreaker Giant next turn and win. Bad trade. Leaf 2 & 3 (one Goblin blocks): Keeps Baloth at 3/4, trades favorably (1/1 for 1/4 health), but I still win next turn with Giant. Leaf 4 (all block): Catastrophic for opponent—loses Baloth entirely, both creatures die, clears my board but gives me unblocked Giant casting next turn. Opponent has no viable path forward in any scenario, but no-blocks preserves the most future options.

Pass upkeep. Opponent at 9 life with only summoning-sick Rumbling Baloth (now untapped but already attacked). My hand has Bonebreaker Giant (4R cost), board has 4 untapped Mountains, Piker (3/2), 2 Goblin Tokens (1/1 each). Next phase: cast Giant, attack with all creatures for 3+1+1+4 = 9 unblocked damage. Lethal achieved turn 11.

Pass priority. Game is won. Opponent at 9 life, no defenses. Hand now contains 2 Bonebreaker Giants (drew additional Giant during draw step). Will proceed to main phase, cast Giant, attack with Piker (3) + 2 Tokens (2) + Giant (4) = 9 damage lethal. Victory confirmed.

Tap first Mountain for red mana. Building toward 4R to cast Bonebreaker Giant for lethal attack. Opponent at 9 life, will take 9 damage from Piker (3) + Token (1) + Token (1) + Giant (4), achieving lethal victory this turn.
Tap second Mountain for red mana. Building toward 4R for Giant cast. Two mana generated, two Mountains remain untapped. Lethal imminent.
Tap third Mountain for red mana. Three mana generated, one Mountain remains untapped. One more tap needed for 4R Giant cast.
Tap fourth and final Mountain for red mana. Now have 4R generated. Ready to cast Bonebreaker Giant (4R) for lethal attack.

attack-all (leaf 1) is optimal: deals 5 damage to bring opponent to 4 life, guaranteeing lethal next turn when all creatures recover and attack again (3+1+1=5 damage, exact lethal). hold-Token variants (leaves 3-4) also guarantee lethal but leave opponent at 5 life instead of 4, requiring opponent to take exactly 5 damage next turn with no margin for error. hold-Piker (leaf 2) reaches opponent at 7 life, requiring 3 turns for lethal. attack-none (leaf 0) stalls and allows opponent to stabilize with their 5 untapped forests. Opponent at 4 life cannot survive another turn regardless of cards played.

Pass to Main Phase. Plan: attack with Piker + Tokens (Baloth blocks Piker for 3 damage, takes 2 unblocked damage, opponent to 2 life). Then cast Bonebreaker Giant (4R) in postcombat main phase. Next turn attack with Giant (4) + Tokens (1+1) = 6 damage for lethal.
Pass to Main Phase. Drew a Mountain (now have 3 cards: 2 Giants + 1 Mountain). Ready to proceed with plan: attack with Piker + Tokens, then cast Giant postcombat.

Pass to combat. No need to play additional lands or tap mana now. Execute attack sequence: declare Piker + Tokens as attackers (5 damage potential). Opponent blocks Piker with untapped Baloth, Piker dies, Tokens deal 2 unblocked damage (opponent to 2 life). Then cast Bonebreaker Giant (4R) in postcombat main phase for lethal setup next turn.
Pass to Declare Attackers step. Ready to attack with Piker + both Tokens for maximum damage.

attack-all (leaves 1-3) is optimal: leads to lethal in most scenarios. Leaf 2 (unblocked, opp to -1) and Leaf 3 (opp blocks Token, opp to 0) are instant wins (score 100). Leaf 1 (opp blocks Piker, opp to 2) leaves opponent at 2 life but we cast Giant postcombat + attack next turn for guaranteed lethal (score 90). hold[Token] (leaves 7-9, 10-12) gives lethal scenarios but slightly lower probability; leaves 8/11 (opp to 1) are 95, leaves 9/12 (unblocked lethal) are 100. hold[Piker] (leaves 4-6) only deals 2 damage unblocked (opp to 2, score 90) or blocked (opp to 3, score 70). attack-none (leaf 0) makes no progress (opp stays at 4, score 20).

Pass to allow combat to resolve. Creatures have been declared as attackers (all three tapped). After opponent declares blockers and combat resolves, we'll have postcombat main phase to cast Bonebreaker Giant with our 4 untapped Mountains for lethal setup.

Pass priority to opponent for blocker declaration. Only opponent's untapped Baloth (with summoning sickness) can block; tapped Baloth cannot. After opponent blocks and combat resolves, move to postcombat main phase to cast Bonebreaker Giant.

Pass through Combat Damage phase. Combat resolved: Piker blocked by Baloth (both died/took damage), 2 Tokens dealt 2 unblocked damage (opponent 4→2 life). Goblin Piker is now in graveyard. Move to postcombat main phase to cast Bonebreaker Giant (4R) for lethal setup next turn.
Pass through End of Combat. Moving to postcombat main phase to cast Bonebreaker Giant (4R) for lethal setup next turn.
Tap first Mountain for red mana. Need 4R total to cast Bonebreaker Giant. Will tap remaining Mountains on subsequent decisions to generate sufficient mana, then cast Giant for lethal setup next turn.
Tap second Mountain for red mana. Now have 2R. Need 2 more for the 4R cast cost. Continue tapping Mountains.
Tap third Mountain for red mana. Now have 3R. Need 1 more R for the 4R cast cost.
Tap fourth and final Mountain for red mana. Now have 4R total. Ready to cast Bonebreaker Giant with full mana available.
Pass priority. Have 4R mana in pool from tapped Mountains. Ready to cast Bonebreaker Giant. Passing moves to spell resolution or next phase where Giant cast will be confirmed/resolved.

Pass upkeep. Critical: game has advanced to Turn 15. I took 8 damage (12→4 life) from opponent's Turn 14 attacks, and opponent has played a third Rumbling Baloth. Despite setback, I'm still close to victory: opponent at 2 life, I have 2 untapped Tokens that can attack for 2 damage = lethal this turn. Move to main phase to execute winning attack.

Pass through Draw phase. Drew Shock instant (2 damage to any target). Moving to Precombat Main Phase to cast Shock on opponent for exact lethal: opponent at 2 life, Shock deals 2 damage = win. (Alternatively could attack with 2 Tokens for same result, but Shock is instant spell with no interactivity risk.)
Cast Shock instantly for 2 damage to opponent. Opponent at 2 life - 2 damage = 0 life = LETHAL. Game over, victory! Shock costs only {R}, easily paid from untapped Mountains.
Target player B (opponent) with Shock. Opponent at 2 life, Shock deals 2 damage, opponent goes to 0 life = VICTORY!

Pass priority. Shock spell is on the stack (cast and targeted opponent player). Pass allows opponent priority to respond, but with no instant-speed effects available to them, Shock will resolve: 2 damage to opponent at 2 life = 0 life = GAME OVER. VICTORY!
